rv.q: "A Bronx Tale" is a wildly uneven show — some parts feel just ridiculous in the broadness of their strokes, others entirely charming.
The musical is handsome and reasonably well performed, but lacks the subtlety to raise questions seriously.
A pleasant but unexceptional musical adaptation of a beloved story.
A Bronx Tale: The Musical is a heartfelt coming-of-age story that successfully translates the beloved film to the Broadway stage with strong performances and memorable musical numbers.
A Bronx Tale is a show that knows exactly what it wants to be and executes that vision with considerable skill and heart.
Too many of the songs are inconsequential, which serves to dilute those ingratiating, low-brow, mob-infused charms which won audiences over in the first (and second) place.
Nevertheless an entertaining crowd-pleaser and a poignant piece of theater.
Chances are this Bronx Tale won’t move you to tears, but Trujillo ensures that it will at least move you a little.
But they haven’t dug especially deep in the imagination department, either.
While there are good things in the musical, it comes across as routine and predictable.
On those occasions, though, they did not have to contend with a score that’s more Disney than the Bronx.
A Bronx Tale is ultimately much better (and more inexpensively experienced) as a movie.
